nodes.name: Spectral $\kappa$-approximation
nodes.statement: $H$ is a $\kappa$-approximation of $G$ if for all $x \in \R^V$, $x^T L_G x \le x^T L_H x \le \kappa \cdot x^T L_G x$, where $L_G, L_H$ are the Laplacian matrices.
nodes.statement_clean: H spectrally approximates G within factor kappa via the Laplacian quadratic form on every vector.

nodes.name: Signed edge-vertex incidence matrix and weighted Laplacian
nodes.section: 2.1 The Incidence Matrix and the Laplacian
nodes.statement: For an oriented weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$, $B_{m\times n}$ has $B(e,v)=1$ if $v$ is $e$'s head, $-1$ if $v$ is $e$'s tail, $0$ otherwise; with $W=\mathrm{diag}(w_e)$, the Laplacian is $L=B^T W B$.

nodes.name: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse of the Laplacian
nodes.statement: If $L=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\lambda_i u_i u_i^T$ is the spectral decomposition of $L$ on its image, then $L^{+}=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{1}{\lambda_i} u_i u_i^T$, and $L L^{+}=L^{+} L$ is the projector onto $\im(L)=\ker(L)^{\perp}$.

nodes.name: Upper and Lower Barrier Potentials $\Phi^u, \Phi_l$
nodes.statement: For a symmetric matrix $A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ and reals $u, l$: $\Phi^u(A) \defeq \tr(uI-A)^{-1} = \sum_i \frac{1}{u-\lambda_i}$ (upper) and $\Phi_l(A) \defeq \tr(A-lI)^{-1} = \sum_i \frac{1}{\lambda_i - l}$ (lower).
nodes.statement_clean: Two trace-based potentials measuring how close eigenvalues are to upper and lower barriers.

nodes.name: Main Theorem: Twice-Ramanujan Sparsifier Existence
nodes.statement: For every $d>1$ and every undirected weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$ on $n$ vertices, there exists a weighted subgraph $H=(V,F,\tilde{w})$ with $\lceil d(n-1) \rceil$ edges such that $x^T L_G x \le x^T L_H x \le \left(\frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}\right) x^T L_G x$ for every $x \in \R^V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Every weighted graph admits a linear-sized spectral sparsifier with twice-Ramanujan condition number.
assumptions: $G=(V,E,w)$ is an undirected weighted graph on $n$ vertices
conclusions: There exists a weighted subgraph $H=(V,F,\tilde{w})$ with at most $\lceil d(n-1)\rceil$ edges
$x^T L_G x \le x^T L_H x \le \left(\frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}\right) x^T L_G x$ for every $x \in \R^V$

nodes.name: Linear-Algebraic Sparsification Theorem
nodes.statement: Suppose $d>1$ and $\v_1,\ldots,\v_m \in \R^n$ satisfy $\sum_{i\le m}\v_i\v_i^T = \id_{\R^n}$. Then there exist scalars $s_i \ge 0$ with $|\{i : s_i \ne 0\}| \le dn$ such that $\id_{\R^n} \preceq \sum_{i\le m} s_i \v_i \v_i^T \preceq \left(\frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}\right) \id_{\R^n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any isotropic set of vectors admits a sparse non-negative reweighting whose outer-product sum is well-conditioned.

nodes.name: Sherman-Morrison Formula
nodes.statement: If $A$ is a nonsingular $n\times n$ matrix and $\v$ is a vector, then $(A+\v\v^T)^{-1} = A^{-1} - \frac{A^{-1}\v\v^T A^{-1}}{1+\v^T A^{-1}\v}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Golub & Van Loan, Matrix Computations, 3rd ed., Sec. 2.1.3

nodes.name: Matrix Determinant Lemma
nodes.statement: If $A$ is nonsingular and $\v$ is a vector, then $\det(A+\v\v^T) = \det(A)(1+\v^T A^{-1}\v)$.

nodes.name: Upper Barrier Shift
nodes.statement: Suppose $\lmax(A)<u$, $\v$ a vector. If $\frac{1}{t} \ge \frac{\v^T((u+\deltaU)I-A)^{-2}\v}{\Phi^u(A)-\Phi^{u+\deltaU}(A)} + \v^T((u+\deltaU)I-A)^{-1}\v \defeq U_A(\v)$, then $\Phi^{u+\deltaU}(A+t\v\v^T) \le \Phi^u(A)$ and $\lmax(A+t\v\v^T)<u+\deltaU$.
nodes.statement_clean: If we add t v v^T with t small enough (in terms of U_A(v)) and shift the upper barrier by deltaU, the upper potential does not increase.

nodes.name: Lower Barrier Shift
nodes.statement: Suppose $\lmin(A)>l$, $\Phi_l(A) \le 1/\deltaL$, and $\v$ is a vector. If $0 < \frac{1}{t} \le \frac{\v^T(A-(l+\deltaL)I)^{-2}\v}{\Phi_{l+\deltaL}(A)-\Phi_l(A)} - \v^T(A-(l+\deltaL)I)^{-1}\v \defeq L_A(\v)$, then $\Phi_{l+\deltaL}(A+t\v\v^T) \le \Phi_l(A)$ and $\lmin(A+t\v\v^T) > l+\deltaL$.

nodes.name: Both Barriers Lemma
nodes.statement: If $\lmax(A)<u$, $\lmin(A)>l$, $\Phi^u(A)\le \epsU$, $\Phi_l(A)\le \epsL$, and $0 \le \frac{1}{\deltaU}+\epsU \le \frac{1}{\deltaL}-\epsL$, then there exist an index $i$ and positive $t$ with $L_A(\v_i) \ge 1/t \ge U_A(\v_i)$, $\lmax(A+t\v_i\v_i^T)<u+\deltaU$, and $\lmin(A+t\v_i\v_i^T)>l+\deltaL$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under matched-barrier parameter conditions, some single rank-one update advances both barriers without raising either potential.

nodes.name: Expander Mixing Property for spectral approximations of $K_n$
nodes.statement: If $L_H$ $(1+\epsilon)$-approximates $L_G$ where $G$ is the complete graph on $V$, then for every disjoint $S, T \subseteq V$: $\left| w(S,T) - (1+\epsilon/2)|S||T| \right| \le n(\epsilon/2)\sqrt{|S||T|}$, where $w(S,T)$ is the sum of edge weights between $S$ and $T$.
assumptions: $L_H$ is the Laplacian of a weighted graph $(V,E,w)$

nodes.name: Lower Bound for Approximating the Complete Graph
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be the complete graph on $V$, $H=(V,E,w)$ a weighted graph on $n$ vertices with a vertex of degree $d$. If $H$ $\kappa$-approximates $G$, then $\kappa \ge 1 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{d}} - O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{d}}{n}\right)$.

nodes.name: Lower-potential Cauchy-Schwartz inequality
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_i > l$ for all $i$, $0 \le \sum_i (\lambda_i - l)^{-1} \le \epsL$, and $1/\deltaL - \epsL \ge 0$, then $\frac{\sum_i (\lambda_i - l - \deltaL)^{-2}}{\sum_i (\lambda_i - l - \deltaL)^{-1} - \sum_i (\lambda_i - l)^{-1}} - \sum_i \frac{1}{\lambda_i - l - \deltaL} \ge \frac{1}{\deltaL} - \sum_i \frac{1}{\lambda_i - l}$.

nodes.name: Kadison-Singer Conjecture (Weaver's discrepancy formulation)
nodes.statement: There exist universal constants $\epsilon>0$, $\delta>0$, $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that: if $\v_1,\ldots,\v_m \in \R^n$ satisfy $\|\v_i\| \le \delta$ for all $i$ and $\sum_{i\le m}\v_i\v_i^T = I$, then there is a partition $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for which $\|\sum_{i\in X_j}\v_i\v_i^T\| \le 1-\epsilon$ for every $j$.
conclusions: There exist universal $\epsilon,\delta,r$ and a partition $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ with $\|\sum_{i\in X_j}\v_i\v_i^T\|\le 1-\epsilon$

nodes.name: Ramanujan Eigenvalue Bound (cited)
nodes.statement: $d$-regular Ramanujan graphs $H$ have all non-zero Laplacian eigenvalues in $[d - 2\sqrt{d-1}, d + 2\sqrt{d-1}]$, so a scaled Ramanujan graph $\kappa$-approximates the complete graph on $n$ vertices with $\kappa = \frac{d+2\sqrt{d-1}}{d-2\sqrt{d-1}}$.
conclusions: Non-zero Laplacian eigenvalues of $H$ lie in $[d-2\sqrt{d-1}, d+2\sqrt{d-1}]$
Scaled $H$ achieves $\kappa = \frac{d+2\sqrt{d-1}}{d-2\sqrt{d-1}}$ vs the complete graph

nodes.name: Alon-Boppana Lower Bound (cited)
nodes.statement: No $d$-regular unweighted graph $\kappa$-approximates the complete graph for $\kappa$ asymptotically better than $\frac{d+2\sqrt{d-1}}{d-2\sqrt{d-1}} = 1 + \frac{4}{\sqrt{d}} + O(1/d)$.
assumptions: $H$ is a $d$-regular unweighted graph on $n$ vertices

nodes.name: Twice-Ramanujan condition number
nodes.statement: $\kappa = \frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}$ is the spectral approximation factor achieved by the construction.

nodes.name: Characteristic polynomial under rank-one update
nodes.statement: $p_{A+\v\v^T}(x) = p_A(x)\left(1 - \sum_j \frac{\langle \v, u_j\rangle^2}{x - \lambda_j}\right)$, where $\lambda_j, u_j$ are eigenpairs of $A$.

nodes.name: Average-vector update generates Laguerre polynomials
nodes.statement: Starting from $A=0$ and adding the average vector $\v_{\textsf{avg}}$ repeatedly gives $p_k(x)=(I-(1/m)D)^k x^n$, the associated Laguerre polynomials, whose largest-to-smallest zero ratio after $k=dn$ steps equals $\frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}$.

nodes.name: Deterministic Greedy Barrier Sparsification Algorithm
nodes.statement: Iteratively builds a sparse non-negative reweighting $A^{(q)} = \sum_q t_q \v_{i_q}\v_{i_q}^T$ by greedily picking, at each step, an index $i$ and weight $t$ that satisfies the upper- and lower-barrier shift conditions, terminating after $Q=dn$ rank-one updates.
output: Non-negative weights $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ with at most $dn$ nonzero entries
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize: A^(0) = 0; deltaL = 1; epsL = 1/sqrt(d); l_0 = -n/epsL; deltaU = (sqrt(d)+1)/(sqrt(d)-1); epsU = (sqrt(d)-1)/(d+sqrt(d)); u_0 = n/epsU. For q = 0 to dn-1: pick any i with L_{A^(q)}(v_i) >= U_{A^(q)}(v_i); choose t with L_{A^(q)}(v_i) >= 1/t >= U_{A^(q)}(v_i); set A^(q+1) = A^(q) + t v_i v_i^T; advance barriers u <- u+deltaU, l <- l+deltaL. Return scalars s_i obtained from the choices.

nodes.name: Spectral Graph Sparsification Problem
nodes.statement: Given a weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$ on $n$ vertices and a parameter $\kappa$, find a sparse weighted subgraph $H=(V,F,\tilde{w})$ with as few edges as possible such that $x^T L_G x \le x^T L_H x \le \kappa \cdot x^T L_G x$ for all $x \in \R^V$.

nodes.name: Reduction matches Spielman-Srivastava up to randomization
nodes.statement: The reduction from graph sparsification to the linear-algebraic Theorem 3.1 is essentially the one used in Spielman-Srivastava 2008, except that the random Rudelson sampling is replaced by a deterministic selection of $O(n)$ columns via Theorem 3.1.

nodes.name: Algorithm running time
nodes.statement: Computing the vectors $\v_i$ takes $O(n^2 m)$; each iteration costs $O(n^3)$ for matrix inverses plus $O(n^2 m)$ to evaluate $U_A(\v_i), L_A(\v_i)$ over edges; with $dn$ iterations the total time is $O(d n^3 m)$.

nodes.name: Conditional implication of strengthened Theorem 3.1 to Kadison-Singer
nodes.statement: If a variant of Theorem 3.1 with $\|\v_i\| \le \delta$ guaranteed all nonzero $s_i$ equal to a constant $\beta$ with $\kappa < \beta$, the Kadison-Singer conjecture (Weaver formulation) would follow with $r=2$ and $\epsilon = \min\{1-\kappa/\beta,\, 1/\beta\}$.

nodes.name: Sparsifiers of the Complete Graph as Weighted Expanders
nodes.statement: Applied to $G = K_n$, the construction yields irregular weighted graphs $H$ of average degree $d$ that are expanders: weighted degrees lie in $[n,(1+\epsilon)n]$ and $H$ satisfies the Expander Mixing Property of Lemma 4.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (reduction to Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 3.1 to the columns $\v_i$ of $V = (L_G^{+})^{1/2} B^T W^{1/2}$ on $\im(L_G)$, then translate the resulting matrix inequalities to a Laplacian inequality on $H$ via Courant-Fischer.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1 (barrier-function construction)
nodes.statement: Choose parameters $\deltaU, \deltaL, \epsU, \epsL, u_0, l_0$ satisfying Lemma 3.5; iteratively apply Lemma 3.5 to extend $A^{(q)}$ for $Q=dn$ steps; bound $\lmax/\lmin$ of $A^{(Q)}$ by $\frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Upper Barrier Shift Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Sherman-Morrison to expand $\Phi^{u+\deltaU}(A+t\v\v^T)$, rearrange to express the difference $\Phi^{u+\deltaU}(A+t\v\v^T) - \Phi^u(A)$ as a single rational expression in $t$, and show it is non-positive for $1/t \ge U_A(\v)$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Lower Barrier Shift Lemma
nodes.statement: Use $\Phi_l(A) \le 1/\deltaL$ to first show $\lmin(A) > l + \deltaL$, then proceed as in the upper case via Sherman-Morrison and rearrangement.

nodes.name: Proof of the Both Barriers Lemma
nodes.statement: Show $\sum_i U_A(\v_i) \le 1/\deltaU + \epsU$ and $\sum_i L_A(\v_i) \ge 1/\deltaL - \epsL$ using $\sum_i \v_i\v_i^T = I$ and Claim 3.6, then combine with the parameter inequality to conclude existence of $i$ with $L_A(\v_i) \ge U_A(\v_i)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.6 (lower-potential Cauchy-Schwartz)
nodes.statement: Algebraic rearrangement reduces the inequality to $\deltaL \sum_i \frac{1}{(\lambda_i-l-\deltaL)^2(\lambda_i-l)} \ge (\deltaL \sum_i \frac{1}{(\lambda_i-l-\deltaL)(\lambda_i-l)})^2$, which follows by Cauchy-Schwartz and the assumed bounds on $\sum (\lambda_i-l)^{-1}$ and $1/\deltaL - \epsL$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1 (Expander Mixing Property)
nodes.statement: Write $L_H = (1+\epsilon/2) L_G + M$ where $\|M\| \le n\epsilon/2$, evaluate $-w(S,T) = x^T L_H y$ on indicator vectors $x,y$, and bound $|x^T M y| \le \|M\|\|x\|\|y\|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.2 (lower bound)
nodes.statement: Construct test vectors $x, y$ centered on the degree-$d$ vertex with $\pm 1/\sqrt{d}$ on its neighbors, compute the ratio $y^T L_H y / x^T L_H x$ in terms of the weighted degrees, project onto $\bvec{1}^{\perp}$, and rearrange.

nodes.name: Set up isotropic columns from the Laplacian
nodes.statement: Restrict to $\im(L_G) \cong \R^{n-1}$ and define $V = (L_G^+)^{1/2} B^T W^{1/2}$; verify $\sum_i \v_i \v_i^T = VV^T = \id_{\im(L_G)}$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.1 to the columns
nodes.statement: Use Theorem 3.1 to obtain scalars $s_i \ge 0$ supported on $\le dn$ indices with $\id_{\im(L_G)} \preceq VSV^T \preceq \kappa\, \id_{\im(L_G)}$, where $S = \mathrm{diag}(s_i)$.

nodes.name: Translate to a Laplacian via Courant-Fischer
nodes.statement: Set $L_H = B^T W^{1/2} S W^{1/2} B$ and apply Courant-Fischer to convert the matrix-inequality on $VSV^T$ into $1 \le x^T L_H x / x^T L_G x \le \kappa$ for all $x \perp \bvec{1}$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Choose parameters satisfying the Both Barriers condition
nodes.statement: Set $\deltaL=1$, $\epsL=1/\sqrt{d}$, $l_0=-n/\epsL$, $\deltaU=(\sqrt{d}+1)/(\sqrt{d}-1)$, $\epsU=(\sqrt{d}-1)/(d+\sqrt{d})$, $u_0=n/\epsU$, and verify $1/\deltaU+\epsU = 1-1/\sqrt{d} = 1/\deltaL-\epsL$ so condition (3.bothcond) holds.

nodes.name: Iterate rank-one updates via Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: Starting from $A^{(0)}=0$, repeatedly apply Lemma 3.5 to find $\v_i$ and $t \ge 0$ with $L_{A^{(q)}}(\v_i) \ge 1/t \ge U_{A^{(q)}}(\v_i)$, set $A^{(q+1)}=A^{(q)}+t\v_i\v_i^T$, run for $Q=dn$ steps.

nodes.name: Bound the condition number after $dn$ steps
nodes.statement: Compute $\lmax(A^{(dn)})/\lmin(A^{(dn)}) \le (n/\epsU + dn\deltaU)/(-n/\epsL + dn\deltaL) = (d+2\sqrt{d}+1)/(d-2\sqrt{d}+1)$, the desired bound.

nodes.name: Expand updated upper potential via Sherman-Morrison
nodes.statement: Let $u' = u+\deltaU$. Sherman-Morrison gives $\Phi^{u'}(A+t\v\v^T) = \Phi^{u'}(A) + \frac{t \v^T(u'I-A)^{-2}\v}{1 - t\v^T(u'I-A)^{-1}\v}$.

nodes.name: Compare to $\Phi^u(A)$ and bound by $U_A(\v)$
nodes.statement: Rewrite as $\Phi^u(A) - (\Phi^u(A) - \Phi^{u'}(A)) + \frac{\v^T(u'I-A)^{-2}\v}{1/t - \v^T(u'I-A)^{-1}\v}$; the last term is finite for $1/t \ge U_A(\v)$, and substituting yields $\Phi^{u'}(A+t\v\v^T) \le \Phi^u(A)$.

nodes.name: Conclude no eigenvalue crosses the upper barrier
nodes.statement: If some $t' \le t$ produced $\lmax(A+t'\v\v^T) = u'$, then $\Phi^{u'}(A+t'\v\v^T)$ would blow up; since it is finite, $\lmax(A+t\v\v^T) < u+\deltaU$.

nodes.name: Show $\lmin(A) > l + \deltaL$
nodes.statement: From $\lmin(A) > l$ and $\Phi_l(A) \le 1/\deltaL$, deduce $\lmin(A) - l \ge \deltaL$, so for any $t > 0$, $\lmin(A+t\v\v^T) > l+\deltaL$.

nodes.name: Expand updated lower potential via Sherman-Morrison
nodes.statement: With $l' = l+\deltaL$, Sherman-Morrison yields $\Phi_{l'}(A+t\v\v^T) = \Phi_{l}(A) + (\Phi_{l'}(A) - \Phi_{l}(A)) - \frac{\v^T(A-l'I)^{-2}\v}{1/t + \v^T(A-l'I)^{-1}\v}$.

nodes.name: Bound by $L_A(\v)$
nodes.statement: Rearrangement shows $\Phi_{l'}(A+t\v\v^T) \le \Phi_l(A)$ exactly when $1/t \le L_A(\v)$.

nodes.name: Bound $\sum_i U_A(\v_i)$ from above
nodes.statement: Using $\sum_i \v_i \v_i^T = I$, $\tr$-linearity, and $\sum_i (u-\lambda_i)^{-1}(u+\deltaU-\lambda_i)^{-1} \ge \sum_i (u+\deltaU-\lambda_i)^{-2}$, derive $\sum_i U_A(\v_i) \le 1/\deltaU + \Phi^u(A) \le 1/\deltaU + \epsU$.

nodes.name: Bound $\sum_i L_A(\v_i)$ from below using Claim 3.6
nodes.statement: Symmetrically expand $\sum_i L_A(\v_i)$ and apply Claim 3.6 (lower-potential Cauchy-Schwartz) to obtain $\sum_i L_A(\v_i) \ge 1/\deltaL - \epsL$.

nodes.name: Combine to get existence of suitable $i, t$
nodes.statement: By the parameter assumption, $\sum_i U_A(\v_i) \le 1/\deltaU + \epsU \le 1/\deltaL - \epsL \le \sum_i L_A(\v_i)$, so some $i$ has $L_A(\v_i) \ge U_A(\v_i)$; pick any $1/t$ in between and apply Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4.

nodes.name: Reduce to a clean polynomial inequality
nodes.statement: Multiply through by the denominators (positive by the assumption $\deltaL \le 1/\epsL \le \lambda_i - l$), rearrange, and identify the goal $\deltaL \sum_i (\lambda_i-l-\deltaL)^{-2}(\lambda_i-l)^{-1} \ge (\deltaL \sum_i ((\lambda_i-l-\deltaL)(\lambda_i-l))^{-1})^2$.

nodes.name: Apply Cauchy-Schwartz
nodes.statement: Cauchy-Schwartz on the products $((\lambda_i-l-\deltaL)\sqrt{\lambda_i-l})^{-1}$ and $\sqrt{\lambda_i-l}^{\,-1}$ gives the squared sum $\le (\deltaL \sum (\lambda_i-l)^{-1})(\deltaL \sum (\lambda_i-l-\deltaL)^{-2}(\lambda_i-l)^{-1})$.

nodes.name: Use $\sum (\lambda_i-l)^{-1}\le\epsL$ and $\deltaL\epsL\le 1$
nodes.statement: Substitute $\sum (\lambda_i-l)^{-1}\le\epsL$ and use $\deltaL\epsL \le 1$ (since $1/\deltaL - \epsL \ge 0$) to drop the leading factor, yielding the desired inequality.

nodes.name: Decompose $L_H = (1+\epsilon/2) L_G + M$
nodes.statement: From $-(\epsilon/2) L_G \preceq L_H - (1+\epsilon/2)L_G \preceq (\epsilon/2) L_G$ and $\|L_G\| \le n$, write $L_H = (1+\epsilon/2) L_G + M$ with $\|M\| \le n\epsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Evaluate quadratic forms on indicator vectors
nodes.statement: For indicator vectors $x = \mathbf{1}_S, y = \mathbf{1}_T$ with $S \cap T = \emptyset$, $-w(S,T) = x^T L_H y$ and $x^T L_G y = -|S||T|$ (since $G = K_n$).

nodes.name: Bound the residual $x^T M y$
nodes.statement: $|x^T M y| \le \|M\|\|x\|\|y\| \le n(\epsilon/2)\sqrt{|S||T|}$, which gives the claimed two-sided bound on $|w(S,T) - (1+\epsilon/2)|S||T||$.

nodes.name: Construct test vectors $x, y$ around the degree-$d$ vertex
nodes.statement: Let $v_0$ be the vertex of degree $d$ with neighbours $v_1,\ldots,v_d$; define $x(v_0)=y(v_0)=1$, $x(v_i)=1/\sqrt{d}$, $y(v_i)=-1/\sqrt{d}$ for $i \ge 1$, and zero elsewhere.

nodes.name: Compute the ratio $y^T L_H y / x^T L_H x$
nodes.statement: Expanding $L_H$ on $x, y$ and using the bound $\sum_i (\delta_i + w_i)/d / \sum_i w_i \le \kappa$ (from $\kappa$-approximation of weighted degrees) gives the ratio $\ge (1 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{d}(1+\kappa)})/(1 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{d}(1+\kappa)})$.

nodes.name: Project onto $\bvec{1}^{\perp}$ and bound norm correction
nodes.statement: Subtracting the $\bvec{1}$ components yields $\|x^*\|^2/\|y^*\|^2 = 1 - O(\sqrt{d}/n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Solve for $\kappa$
nodes.statement: Combining the ratio and norm-correction bounds with $y^{*T}L_H y^*/x^{*T}L_H x^* \le \kappa$ and rearranging yields $\kappa \ge 1 + 2/\sqrt{d} - O(\sqrt{d}/n)$.

nodes.name: Initialize matrix and barrier parameters
nodes.statement: Set $A^{(0)} = 0$, $\deltaL = 1$, $\epsL = 1/\sqrt{d}$, $l_0 = -n/\epsL$, $\deltaU = (\sqrt{d}+1)/(\sqrt{d}-1)$, $\epsU = (\sqrt{d}-1)/(d+\sqrt{d})$, $u_0 = n/\epsU$, $q = 0$.

nodes.name: Greedy update loop
nodes.statement: While $q < dn$: pick any index $i$ with $L_{A^{(q)}}(\v_i) \ge U_{A^{(q)}}(\v_i)$ (exists by Lemma 3.5); choose $t > 0$ with $L_{A^{(q)}}(\v_i) \ge 1/t \ge U_{A^{(q)}}(\v_i)$; set $A^{(q+1)} = A^{(q)} + t\v_i\v_i^T$ and accumulate the weight $s_i \mathrel{+}= t$; advance $u \leftarrow u+\deltaU$, $l \leftarrow l+\deltaL$, $q \leftarrow q+1$.

nodes.name: Return sparse weights
nodes.statement: Return $\{s_i\}_{i=1}^m$; at most $dn$ entries are non-zero, and $\id \preceq \sum_i s_i\v_i\v_i^T \preceq \frac{d+1+2\sqrt{d}}{d+1-2\sqrt{d}}\,\id$.
